facts.fact: Adwave states that TV advertising went from a $50,000 minimum to a $50 minimum.
facts.quote: **TV advertising went from $50,000 minimum to $50 minimum.**

facts.fact: Adwave states that channels requiring six-figure budgets five years ago are now accessible to anyone, and that a business with $50 and an internet connection can access enterprise-only marketing channels.
facts.quote: the marketing channels that used to be "enterprise only" are now accessible to any business with $50 and an internet connection.

facts.fact: Adwave states that streaming TV campaigns on its platform start at $50.
facts.quote: Starting at $50, you can run campaigns that put your brand alongside the biggest advertisers in the world.

facts.fact: Adwave gives an example of a restaurant running a $500/month TV campaign targeting its neighborhood, which it says gives visibility that used to require $50,000.
facts.quote: A restaurant running a $500/month TV campaign targeting their neighborhood is getting visibility that used to require $50,000.

facts.fact: Adwave states that professional video production that once required a $10,000 shoot can now be done with AI tools from a website, without production crews.
facts.quote: No production crews, no $10,000 shoots, no weeks of editing.

facts.fact: Adwave's article describes a targeted local advertising radius of 10 miles around a business.
facts.quote: You can target a 10-mile radius around your business.

facts.fact: Adwave's article is published with a date of July 10, 2025.
AdWave states that CTV advertising is accessible at budgets starting around $50 for small businesses.
facts.quote: With CTV advertising accessible at budgets starting around $50, small businesses can now access the same premium streaming inventory as major corporations.

facts.fact: AdWave's page outlines a 90-day marketing roadmap organized into three monthly phases, with Month 2 covering launch of a multi-channel presence.
